assessment: Three unrestricted tutors — Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor, Diabolic Intent — against four loop halves: that is this deck's consistency engine. A tutor is 'essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck', and here every tutor is a copy of whichever half completes a verified pairing. Natural assembly is 5.4% by turn 6 and 9.4% by turn 10 (goldfish, tutors unmodeled), so the tutors ARE the assembly. The fetch discipline is removal-window profiling: fetch toward the pairing the table's open mana cannot answer — stack 005's all-enchantment Bond+Exquisite against creature-removal seats, a creature half only when the coast is genuinely clear. And remember the second job: against lifegain hate or an assembling lock, the tutors fetch the answer, not the combo.

tutors.notes: Two mana, any card, to hand. The question is never 'what is the best card' — it is 'which half completes a pair the table's held interaction cannot break.' Cite the matrix, then count their open mana.

targets.scenario: A gain-half is sleeved — Exquisite Blood or Bloodthirsty Conqueror on the battlefield — and the draw-go seat keeps passing with mana up.
targets.why: Bond is the lose-half with no body. With Exquisite Blood it assembles stack 005's all-enchantment loop — 26 iterations, deterministic, no per-iteration creature-removal window; with Conqueror it assembles stack 006. Fetch the half instant-speed creature removal cannot touch, hold it hidden, and cast it into the first tapped-out window.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: A lose-half is sleeved — Vito or Sanguine Bond has survived a table rotation — and you want the engine that closes.
targets.why: The gain-half with two living partners: it completes stack 001 with Vito and stack 005 with Bond, and any lifelink connect or Cruel Celebrant death seeds the loop. It is also the resilient gain-half — an enchantment, untouched by every kill spell aimed at your creatures.

citations.quote: essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck

targets.scenario: You are behind: the aggro seat has run you low behind a bigger board, and your drains cannot race it.
targets.why: The asymmetric reset: every non-Vampire gets -X/-X where X is your Vampire count, so it wipes their board and misses your entire army. You keep the eminence tokens, they keep nothing, and the race restarts with you ahead.

targets.scenario: Closing: six-plus attackers plus Sanctum Seeker, the alpha turn is next, and you want it to end the game rather than dent it.
targets.why: The doubler that turns the swing lethal. Stack 003 verified seven attackers under Sanctum Seeker and Bloodletter drain each opponent 14 at declare — before blockers exist — and stack 007 adds another verified 14 per opponent at your end step through Throne of the God-Pharaoh. One fetch converts a good attack into a table-shaking one.

tutors.notes: The additional cost is nearly free — the engine prints the currency. Best body: Bloodghast if a land drop or fetch remains, because it returns on landfall for zero mana; otherwise a spare eminence token. Either death also pays out under Cruel Celebrant, Cordial Vampire, or Grave Pact: the tutor's cost becomes a drain, counters, and an edict on its way to the bin.

targets.scenario: Vito is on the battlefield, the table is tapped out or spent, and the window is open now.
targets.why: Completes stack 001 on the spot — deterministic, 38 iterations from a 2-life seed, retargeted each trigger, unbroken by a mid-loop death. When the open-mana count passes, Intent is Demonic Tutor at a discount you pay with a token you got for free.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: Both boards went wide and theirs is winning the fair fight — you need the board broken on your terms.
targets.why: The scalable sweeper: pay life to set X, sized to kill their board while your lords keep the counters-and-anthem survivors alive. Sacrificing Bloodghast to Intent first costs nothing — it returns on your next land drop, after the dust settles.

targets.scenario: Closing through a stall: the swarm is big enough to win but chump-blockers keep it honest.
targets.why: Choose Vampire and the swarm gains fear — blockable only by artifact and black creatures. The sacrificed token is one fewer attacker, and it does not matter: the rest connect, and stack 003's declare-attackers drain math still fires per attacker.

targets.scenario: A 'players can't gain life' piece landed and the whole 2×2 matrix is dark.
targets.why: The kill that ignores the hate: stack 008 verified 10 damage to each opponent per two-mana Vampire cast through both doublers, with no lifegain anywhere in the line. Indestructible and usually not a creature at this deck's devotion, he also ignores the wrath that seat is holding.

tutors.notes: One mana, instant speed, top of library — not hand. The card arrives on your NEXT draw, so cast it at the end step of the player before you: minimum information leaked, minimum time for a shuffle or surprise mill to take the top. The 2 life is trivial currency in a deck whose engines drain the whole table — but respect it under pressure. At 6 life against a swarm, the honest fetch is the sweeper, not the combo half.

targets.scenario: A gain-half is on the battlefield and your next untap is the assembly window.
targets.why: One mana at their end step sets the resilient lose-half on top; you draw it and cast it into stack 005 or 006's verified loop. Vampiric's discount over Demonic is exactly what keeps the loop's cast mana free on the combo turn.

citations.quote: sequence scary pieces after the table's removal is spent

targets.scenario: The wrath is telegraphed — the control seat passes with 4+ mana and your board is the widest at the table.
targets.why: The total out: life locked, protection from everything, board phased out. Set it the end step before your draw and it is in hand before their sorcery-speed window opens — one mana and 2 life for the disaster policy exactly when the premium is highest.

targets.scenario: Alpha-strike turn next: Edgar is castable, seven attackers ready, and the swing must stick.
targets.why: With Edgar on the battlefield you take both modes — flying, double strike, protection AND lifelink-indestructible — and every lifelink point is a lose-half trigger. Set it at the last end step before yours; the table sees one mana spent and learns nothing.

targets.scenario: Twilight Prophet is on the battlefield with the city's blessing and your upkeep is coming.
targets.why: The wish nobody sees coming. Prophet reveals the top card at your upkeep, drains each opponent for its mana value, and puts it in your hand. A five-mana card on top means each opponent loses 5 and the combo half lands in hand anyway — the tutor recoups its 2 life doubled per opponent and delivers the fetch without spending your draw.

gaps: No tutor puts a card onto the battlefield or fetches at instant speed to play — every assembly crosses at least one turn of exposure, which is why the hidden-hand discipline matters as much as the fetch choice.

Against a resolved 'players can't gain life' effect the tutors can only fetch the answer (Despark, Fracture) or the hate-proof plan (Purphoros) — no tutor line restores the matrix while the piece stands.
The aristocrats-ignition path — a Cruel Celebrant death seeding a full pair — is flagged by the strategic frame as needing a stack scenario; these wishes lean on lifelink connects, the verified seed.
None of the three tutors is mana fixing in practice: burning Demonic Tutor on a land is a losing wish, and the manabase math belongs to Sources Say.
